summary: The note explains "Phantom Tornadoes," nighttime tornadoes named for being poorly detected or undetected in the dark rather than for any difference in how they form. It describes incidents in Eastwood, Cedar Valley and Elkins Ranch in 2023, expert views debunking myths about power and climate change, and gaps in nocturnal detection and warnings. It closes with ongoing research and new technologies such as RTALabs' machine-learning prototype.
one_line: Phantom Tornadoes are nighttime twisters that form like daytime ones but evade detection, prompting calls for better radar, warnings, research and awareness.
key_facts: A "Phantom Tornado" struck the town of Eastwood on September 5, 2023, at 11:40 PM with no prior severe weather alerts, according to the Eastwood Meteorological Office; it caused heavy damage but no deaths.
Phantom Tornadoes do not differ from daytime tornadoes in formation or structure; the name comes from their undetected or poorly detected approach in darkness and limited nocturnal monitoring.
Dr. Harold Geen says there is nothing inherently unique about Phantom Tornadoes and that "The difference lies in our ability to detect and predict them."
A Phantom Tornado hit the farming community of Cedar Valley at 2 AM on October 10, 2023; it was rated EF2 on the Enhanced Fujita scale and caused substantial crop damage.
Cedar Valley farmer Josephine Marks said the sirens didn't go off and there was no warning before the tornado was upon them.

On November 22, 2023, a Phantom Tornado swept through the Smith family's property at Elkins Ranch without a forecasted warning; Arthur Smith said they barely made it to the cellar and never heard the siren.
The National Weather Services has started efforts to improve nocturnal radar technology and public awareness, but progress is slow due to limited budgets and vast areas to cover.
Climatologist Rebecca Sun says blaming climate change alone for Phantom Tornadoes is premature, as the relationship is more complex than direct cause and effect and is still being researched.
Recommended precautions include a good-quality weather radio and subscribing to local weather notifications, though these depend on timely warnings.
RTALabs, a weather prediction tech company, introduced a prototype on February 12, 2024 that uses machine learning to analyze weather patterns and promises better nighttime tornado prediction.
Universities and governmental organizations are collaborating on research into tornado genesis at night.
